name: Dripify
summary: Cloud-based LinkedIn outreach automation — drip sequences of connection requests, messages, InMails and profile views, with configurable daily limits and a built-in email finder.
best_for: sales teams that already run LinkedIn outreach, understand that automation breaches LinkedIn's terms, and accept that risk with their eyes open — the cloud architecture means sequences run with your browser closed and no extension injected into your session
skip_if: your LinkedIn account is not expendable, since a restriction can be permanent and no tool can promise otherwise; or you are tempted by the 75-a-day ceiling, because the vendor's own advice is roughly a fifth of that
honest_knock: Understand what you are buying before the price matters: LinkedIn prohibits this entire product category. Its User Agreement bans using 'bots or other unauthorized automated methods' to 'send or redirect messages', and its prohibited-software page says members using such tools 'risk having their accounts restricted or shut down'. There is no carve-out for cloud tools or low volumes, and Dripify is not an outlier here — every competitor sits on the same side of that line. Dripify's own documentation is candid about the consequence, warning that LinkedIn 'may issue warnings, temporary restrictions, or even permanent bans', and it publishes a recovery procedure for exactly that scenario. Two things follow. First, the advertised ceiling is not a working speed: the app allows up to 75 connection requests a day, while Dripify's own setup guide tells beginners to run 10 to 15, and brand-new accounts 2 to 5, building up 10 to 20 percent a week. Anyone buying on the headline number is buying capacity they are told not to use. Second, Activity Control sits on the $79 Advanced tier. It is the feature Dripify names as its best protection, and it adjusts your pace automatically. On Basic and Pro, safe pacing is your own manual responsibility. And when a vendor writes that a feature 'makes sure your LinkedIn account won't get flagged', read that as a claim about a third party's enforcement decisions that no vendor can actually guarantee.

pricing.plans_source: hand-curated from the vendor's pricing page
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-08-26 on their own pricing page — note that dripify.io now redirects to dripify.com) Four tiers, priced per user: Basic $39, Pro $59 and Advanced $79 per user per month billed annually, plus an Enterprise tier that is quote-only. Month to month the same tiers read $59, $79 and $99 per user; both columns sit in the page and the FAQ repeats all six numbers in words. A 7-day free trial runs without a credit card. So the 'up to 35% off' the toggle advertises is real but front-loaded: you pay a year up front to get it, and the discount shrinks as you go up the range — about 34 percent on Basic, 25 on Pro, 20 on Advanced. What each tier buys is unusually consequential here, and the page now prints the daily quotas instead of calling them 'limited': Basic sends 20 connection requests, 30 messages, 10 Sales Navigator InMails and 100 profile views a day, against 75, 100+, 30 and 200+ on Pro and Advanced. Basic is also capped at one drip campaign; unlimited campaigns and full quotas start at Pro, which adds a dedicated inbox, CSV export and the webhook and HubSpot integrations, and Advanced adds multi-team management, advanced LinkedIn protection, lead tagging, step analytics and evergreen leads. Every tier includes 100 email-finder credits a month and the top-ups are priced openly: 1,000 credits $29, 2,000 $49, 5,000 $69, 10,000 $99. One seat connects one LinkedIn account, so five reps means five seats, and ten or more seats goes through sales. Re-read 10 October 2026: prices and daily quotas unchanged, and Pro now also lists an Open API and an MCP server.

compare_with.name: Expandi
compare_with.why: the closest head-to-head — both are cloud-based with a regional dedicated IP, so the 'cloud versus extension' framing you will read in affiliate roundups does not actually separate them. The real difference is the pricing model: Expandi sells one Business plan with everything included at $99 per user a month, 20 percent off annually, while Dripify tiers both quotas and safety features. Watch the $39-versus-$99 gap that roundups quote — that is Dripify's annual rate against Expandi's monthly one. Month against month it is $59 to $99 versus $99, and at the top of Dripify's range the two cost the same. Both price lists read on 2026-07-24; verify them yourself before you buy.
